Anybody that works around the running shoe world would tell you that nothing is a end-all, be-all solution. The trend for the past few years are shoes are making their sockliners softer to improve step-in feel, which is how a lot of people make their purchases now. Hokas feel good when you try them on, and the average person assumes it will translate. Now it shifts back to maybe hitting those upper bounds for the entry-level runner, in a time where many more people are entry-level. That doesn't mean barefoot shoes are the solution. Everything in moderation, and excess requires balancing. Shoe rotations help mitigate these situations, but seeing someone's first running shoe as the Vomero Premium sparks a visceral reaction in me.
